Should the Planning Commission wish to recommend approvalof the Zoning Map Amendment, the
Commission must make the following findings required in UDC 2.2.1.d. A detailed analysis is below:
1)The application is in accordance with the development policies and physical patterns
identified in the Comprehensive Plan.(UDC2.2.1.d.1)
Plan Cheyenne encourages growth within the Urban Service Boundary and the maximization of
existing infrastructure.This propertyis within the Urban Service Boundary and existing
infrastructure exists in the neighborhoods to the west.There are also opportunities to tieinto

proposed future land use designation is any of the residential zones forthe Urban Residential
areas, and Mixed-use Business Emphasis forthe Mixed-Use Commercial areas. Commercial and
residential zoning may also be appropriate in the Mixed-Use area.
While the proposed AG zone is not consistent with the land uses identified by the Future Land
Use Map, the AG zone is the rough equivalent of the current County zone and would not have
an adverse effect on the potential for the property to develop in accordance with the plans and
policiesof the comprehensive plan in the future.
The proposed zone change complies with review criterion1.

and the proposed AG zone is the City zone most analogous to the current countyzone.
The future land uses anticipated by the Comprehensive Plan and other official plans for this area
anticipate higher-intensity, urban-style uses.While the proposed AG zone is not consistent with
the Future Land Use Map, the AG zone is intended to be able to be used as a‘holding zone'until
future development occurs, and the AGzone is consistent with existing County zoning in the
area.
The proposed zone change for the subject property complies with review criterion 2.

The current CountyA-2zone allows limited development options and is intended for low-
intensity uses. Generally, parcels in this zone district are not expected to connect to urban
services.The proposed AG zone is the City zone most analogousto the current County zone and
also only allows limited development options.However, in order for land uses and development
tobe effectively managed when annexed to the City, a City zone isrequired.
The proposed zone change complies with review criterion3.

Subdivision Standards in Article 4 considering the proposed zoning(UDC 2.2.1.d.4)
The standards of Article 4 have limited applicability to the proposed AG zone, as AG zoned land
